subproblems.title: Smooth cutoff ϑ (= 1 on B_r(0), 0 ≤ ϑ ≤ 1) and the test form ϑ·β
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, r > 0 and β ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, n). Then there exist ϑ : ℝ^P → ℝ and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n) such that: ϑ is continuous with compact support; 0 ≤ ϑ(x) ≤ 1 for all x; ϑ(x) = 1 whenever ‖x‖ < r; and ω(x) = ϑ(x)·β for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (r : ℝ) (β : Covector (Euclid P) n), 0 < r → ∃ (ϑ : Euclid P → ℝ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), Continuous ϑ ∧ HasCompactSupport ϑ ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ ϑ x ∧ ϑ x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x : Euclid P, ‖x‖ < r → ϑ x = 1) ∧ ∀ x, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x = ϑ x • β
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the supplied proof of the selected node (the bump function ϑ and the test form ω_ϑ = ϑ·β), with the radius 3 replaced by an arbitrary r > 0 and the degree 2 by an arbitrary n. The selected node uses it with n = 2 and r = 3.
Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). An n-covector is β ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n, and (c • β)(v) = c·β(v) for c ∈ ℝ. 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) = TestFormOn univ n consists of the forms F : ℝ^P → Covector (Euclid P) n with IsTestForm F, i.e. IsSmoothForm F (ContDiff ℝ ∞ F, where ∞ = ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)) and HasCompactSupport F, together with tsupport F ⊆ univ. The coercion of ⟨F, h⟩ to a DifferentialForm is F.
1. (Bump.) ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional real inner product space, so Mathlib provides HasContDiffBump (Euclid P). Since 0 < r < r + 1, there is a smooth bump function f : ContDiffBump (0 : Euclid P) with rIn = r and rOut = r + 1. Put ϑ := ⇑f : ℝ^P → ℝ.
2. (Properties of ϑ.) From the ContDiffBump API: ϑ is C^k for every k ∈ ℕ∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff), in particular ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ϑ, and ϑ is continuous (ContDiffBump.continuous). For every x, 0 ≤ ϑ(x) (ContDiffBump.nonneg) and ϑ(x) ≤ 1 (ContDiffBump.le_one). ϑ has compact support (ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport; Euclid P is finite-dimensional). Finally ϑ(x) = 1 for every x ∈ closedBall 0 r (ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall, as rIn = r).
3. (ϑ = 1 on the open ball.) If ‖x‖ < r, then dist x 0 = ‖x‖ ≤ r, so x ∈ closedBall 0 r and ϑ(x) = 1 by step 2.
4. (The form.) Let F(x) := ϑ(x) • β. F is smooth: it is the scalar product (ContDiff.smul) of the C^∞ function ϑ (step 2) with the constant map x ↦ β (contDiff_const), so IsSmoothForm F. F has compact support: F = ϑ • (fun _ ↦ β), and HasCompactSupport.smul_right turns HasCompactSupport ϑ into HasCompactSupport F (F(x) = 0 wherever ϑ(x) = 0). Hence IsTestForm F, and tsupport F ⊆ univ holds trivially. So F ∈ testFormOnSubmodule univ n, and ω := ⟨F, ⟨⟨smoothness, compact support⟩, subset_univ _⟩⟩ ∈ TestFormOn univ n.
5. (Conclusion.) By step 2, ϑ is continuous with compact support and values in [0, 1]. By step 3, ϑ(x) = 1 whenever ‖x‖ < r. By definition, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x = F x = ϑ x • β for every x (rfl). This gives all five conjuncts. ∎
Formalization note: this exact statement was proved in a scratch build.
- Bump and smoothness: `let f : ContDiffBump (0 : Euclid P) := ⟨r, r + 1, hr, by linarith⟩` and `have hsm : IsSmoothForm (fun x : Euclid P => f x • β) := (f.contDiff (n := ⊤)).smul contDiff_const`.
- Compact support: `have hcs : HasCompactSupport (fun x : Euclid P => f x • β) := f.hasCompactSupport.smul_right`.
- Membership: `have hmem : (fun x : Euclid P => f x • β) ∈ TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n := ⟨⟨hsm, hcs⟩, subset_univ _⟩`.
- Assembly: `refine ⟨f, ⟨fun x => f x • β, hmem⟩, f.continuous, f.hasCompactSupport, fun x => ⟨f.nonneg, f.le_one⟩, fun x hx => f.one_of_mem_closedBall ?_, fun x => rfl⟩`, closed by `simpa [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right] using hx.le`.
- Under `open scoped ENNReal` the symbol ∞ is ENNReal's top. State smoothness as IsSmoothForm, or with ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), never as `ContDiff ℝ ∞`.
proof_key_steps: Take Mathlib's ContDiffBump f centred at 0 with rIn = r < rOut = r + 1 and put ϑ := f.
The ContDiffBump API makes ϑ smooth, continuous and compactly supported, with 0 ≤ ϑ ≤ 1 and ϑ = 1 on closedBall 0 r ⊇ {‖x‖ < r}.
F := ϑ•β is smooth (a smooth scalar times a constant) with compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right). So F ∈ TestFormOn univ n, and ω := F satisfies ω x = ϑ x • β by rfl.

subproblems.title: Blow-up of a represented current on the form g·β: η_{a,t#}C(ω) = t^{−n}∫ g(η_{a,t}y)·ξ(y)(β) dμ
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), and R an IMRep(univ, n) with R.Represents C; put μ := R.measure and ξ := R.orient. Let a ∈ ℝ^P, t > 0, g : ℝ^P → ℝ, β ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, n), and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n) with ω(x) = g(x)·β for every x. Then currentEval(blowUp C a t, ω) = t^{−n}·∫ g(dilation a t y)·ξ(y)(β) dμ(y).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (a : Euclid P) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t) (g : Euclid P → ℝ) (β : Covector (Euclid P) n) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), R.Represents C → (∀ x, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x = g x • β) → currentEval (blowUp C a t ht.ne') (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) = t⁻¹ ^ n * ∫ y, g (dilation a t y) * R.orient y β ∂R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4 (the currentEval branch) and 5 of the supplied proof of the selected node, for an arbitrary degree n and an arbitrary scalar function g. The selected node uses it with n = 2, g = ϑ and t = t_j.
Notation: η := dilation a t, so η(y) = −(t⁻¹•a) + t⁻¹•y (dilationCLM P t y = t⁻¹•y). μ := R.measure and ξ := R.orient.
Accepted declarations used; both are reused siblings of this decomposition:
- Submission.dtc_blowUp_testForm_corr (key testform_corr);
- Submission.cbr_imRep_measure_basic (key imrep_measure).
1. (η is onto.) For z ∈ ℝ^P put y := a + t•z. Then η(y) = −(t⁻¹•a) + t⁻¹•a + (t⁻¹t)•z = z, because t ≠ 0. Hence η '' univ = univ.
2. (The test-form branch of currentEval.) ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n gives IsTestForm ω (first component of the membership proof). By step 1, tsupport ω ⊆ univ = η '' univ. Call this proof hmem : IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ η '' univ. By definition, currentEval T ω = (if h : IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ V then T ⟨ω, h⟩ else 0) for T ∈ 𝒟_n(V). Here T := blowUp C a t has domain V = η '' univ. The positive branch gives currentEval(blowUp C a t, ω) = blowUp C a t ω̃, where ω̃ := ⟨ω, hmem⟩ ∈ TestFormOn (η '' univ) n has the same underlying form as ω.
3. (Pull-back to C.) Apply Submission.dtc_blowUp_testForm_corr P n univ a t ht.
- Part (a), applied to ω̃, gives ω' ∈ TestFormOn univ n with ω'(y) = ω̃(η(y)) = ω(η(y)) for all y.
- Part (c), with T := C, ω̃ and ω', gives blowUp C a t ω̃ = t⁻¹ ^ n · C(ω').
4. (Representation.) R.Represents C, applied to ω', gives C(ω') = R.action ω'. The last conjunct of Submission.cbr_imRep_measure_basic P n univ R says R.action F = ∫ ξ(y)(F(y)) dμ for every form F. Hence C(ω') = ∫ ξ(y)(ω'(y)) dμ(y).
5. (The integrand.) For every y, step 3 and the hypothesis on ω give ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) = g(η(y))•β. Since ξ(y) = R.orient y is a (continuous) linear map, ξ(y)(g(η(y))•β) = g(η(y))·ξ(y)(β) (map_smul, smul_eq_mul). So the two integrands agree at every point. Hence ∫ ξ(y)(ω'(y)) dμ = ∫ g(η(y))·ξ(y)(β) dμ, by integral_congr_ae with an equality valid everywhere. No integrability is needed, because the integrands are equal functions.
6. Combining steps 2–5: currentEval(blowUp C a t, ω) = blowUp C a t ω̃ = t⁻¹ ^ n · C(ω') = t⁻¹ ^ n · ∫ g(dilation a t y)·R.orient y β dμ(y). ∎
Formalization note: this exact statement was proved in a scratch build, with the two accepted declarations in scope.
- Surjectivity: `have hsurj : dilation a t '' (univ : Set (Euclid P)) = univ := eq_univ_of_forall fun z => ⟨a + t • z, mem_univ _, by simp [dilation, dilationCLM, smul_add, smul_smul, ht.ne']⟩`.
- Membership: `have hmem : IsTestForm (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ∧ tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ dilation a t '' univ := ⟨ω.2.1, by rw [hsurj]; exact subset_univ _⟩`.
- Branch: `rw [currentEval, dite_eq_left hmem]`. `dite_eq_left` is the non-deprecated name of `dif_pos` at this toolchain.
- Pull-back: obtain ⟨ω', hω'⟩ from `(Submission.dtc_blowUp_testForm_corr P n univ a t ht).1 ⟨ω, hmem⟩`, then `rw [(Submission.dtc_blowUp_testForm_corr P n univ a t ht).2.2 C ⟨ω, hmem⟩ ω' hω', hRC ω', (Submission.cbr_imRep_measure_basic P n univ R).2.2.2.2.2.2]`.
- Finish: `congr 1`, then `refine integral_congr_ae (Eventually.of_forall fun y => ?_)` and `simp only [hω', hω, map_smul, smul_eq_mul]`.
proof_key_steps: dilation a t is onto, so ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n is a test form for the domain dilation a t '' univ of blowUp C a t. currentEval therefore takes its positive branch: currentEval(blowUp C a t, ω) = blowUp C a t ⟨ω, _⟩.
dtc_blowUp_testForm_corr (a), (c) give ω' with ω'(y) = ω(dilation a t y) and blowUp C a t ⟨ω, _⟩ = t⁻¹ ^ n · C(ω').
R.Represents C and the last conjunct of cbr_imRep_measure_basic give C(ω') = ∫ R.orient y (ω' y) dμ.
ω'(y) = g(dilation a t y)•β and linearity of R.orient y turn the integrand into g(dilation a t y)·R.orient y β pointwise.

subproblems.title: Single-scale calibration bound for the tilt excess on B_{3t}(a)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and μ a measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K. Let d : ℝ^P → ℝ be μ-a.e.-strongly measurable with |d| ≤ 1 μ-a.e. Let ϑ : ℝ^P → ℝ be continuous with compact support, ϑ ≥ 0, and ϑ(x) = 1 whenever ‖x‖ < 3. Let a ∈ ℝ^P and t > 0. Then (∫⁻_{B_{3t}(a)} ofReal(1 − |d(x)|) dμ(x)) / ofReal(t²) ≤ ofReal(t^{−2}∫ ϑ(dilation a t x) dμ(x) − |t^{−2}∫ ϑ(dilation a t x)·d(x) dμ(x)|).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (d ϑ : Euclid P → ℝ) (a : Euclid P) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable d μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, |d x| ≤ 1) → Continuous ϑ → HasCompactSupport ϑ → (∀ x, 0 ≤ ϑ x) → (∀ x : Euclid P, ‖x‖ < 3 → ϑ x = 1) → (∫⁻ x in ball a (3 * t), ENNReal.ofReal (1 - |d x|) ∂μ) / ENNReal.ofReal (t ^ 2) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (t⁻¹ ^ 2 * ∫ x, ϑ (dilation a t x) ∂μ - |t⁻¹ ^ 2 * ∫ x, ϑ (dilation a t x) * d x ∂μ|)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 6, 7 (the inequality 0 ≤ D_j ≤ A_j − |C_j(ω_ϑ)|) and 8 of the supplied proof of the selected node, at a single scale t. The selected node applies it with μ := R.measure, d := R.orient(·)(β) and t := t_j.
Notation: h(x) := ϑ(dilation a t x), B := ball a (3t), D := ∫ h dμ − |∫ h·d dμ|.
1. (The dilation.) dilation a t x = −(t⁻¹•a) + t⁻¹•x = t⁻¹•(x − a). Let e be x ↦ t⁻¹•x (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero t⁻¹, as t⁻¹ ≠ 0) followed by z ↦ −(t⁻¹•a) + z (Homeomorph.addLeft (−(t⁻¹•a))). Then e is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P, and e(x) = dilation a t x for all x.
2. (h is integrable.) h = ϑ ∘ e is continuous, and HasCompactSupport h holds by HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph. The hypothesis μ(K) < ∞ for compact K is exactly IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ. So h is μ-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). Also h(x) = ϑ(dilation a t x) ≥ 0 for every x.
3. (h = 1 on B.) Let x ∈ B, i.e. ‖x − a‖ < 3t. Then ‖dilation a t x‖ = ‖t⁻¹•(x − a)‖ = t⁻¹‖x − a‖ < 3, using t > 0. Hence h(x) = 1 by the hypothesis on ϑ.
4. (Integrability of the products.) |d| = ‖d‖ is a.e.-strongly measurable. The products h·d and h·|d| are a.e.-strongly measurable, h being continuous. μ-a.e. we have |d| ≤ 1, hence |h·d| = h|d| ≤ h and |h·|d|| = h|d| ≤ h, using h ≥ 0. By Integrable.mono' with the integrable dominating function h, both h·d and h·|d| are μ-integrable. Consequently h(1 − |d|) = h − h|d| is integrable. Moreover h(1 − |d|) ≥ 0 μ-a.e., because 1 − |d| ≥ 0 a.e.
5. (Ball estimate.) B is open, hence measurable, so ∫⁻_B ofReal(1 − |d|) dμ = ∫⁻ 1_B·ofReal(1 − |d|) dμ (lintegral_indicator). Compare the integrands at every x:
- if x ∈ B, then 1_B(x)·ofReal(1 − |d(x)|) = ofReal(1 − |d(x)|) = ofReal(h(x)(1 − |d(x)|)), by step 3;
- if x ∉ B, the left side is 0 ≤ ofReal(h(x)(1 − |d(x)|)).
By lintegral_mono (a pointwise inequality everywhere; no measurability required), ∫⁻_B ofReal(1 − |d|) dμ ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(h(1 − |d|)) dμ. This equals ofReal(∫ h(1 − |d|) dμ) by ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal, the integrand being integrable and a.e. nonnegative by step 4.
6. (Calibration inequality.) By integral_sub (step 4), ∫ h(1 − |d|) dμ = ∫ h dμ − ∫ h|d| dμ. Also |∫ h·d dμ| ≤ ∫ |h·d| dμ = ∫ h|d| dμ, by abs_integral_le_integral_abs and |h·d| = h|d| (h ≥ 0). Therefore ∫ h(1 − |d|) dμ ≤ ∫ h dμ − |∫ h·d dμ| = D.
7. (Rescaling.) Steps 5, 6 and monotonicity of ofReal give ∫⁻_B ofReal(1 − |d|) dμ ≤ ofReal(D). ENNReal division by ofReal(t²) is monotone in the numerator. So the left side of the claim is ≤ ofReal(D)/ofReal(t²) = ofReal(D/t²), by ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos (t² > 0). Finally, since t⁻² > 0, D/t² = t⁻²∫ h dμ − t⁻²|∫ h·d dμ| = t⁻²∫ h dμ − |t⁻²∫ h·d dμ|. With h(x) = ϑ(dilation a t x), this is exactly the argument of ofReal on the right-hand side of the claim. ∎
Formalization note: this exact statement was proved in a scratch build.
- Measure instance: `have : IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ := ⟨fun K hK => hloc K hK⟩`.
- Homeomorphism: `let e : Euclid P ≃ₜ Euclid P := (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero t⁻¹ (inv_ne_zero ht.ne')).trans (Homeomorph.addLeft (-(t⁻¹ • a)))`, with `e x = dilation a t x` by `simp [e, dilation, dilationCLM]`; compact support from `hϑcs.comp_homeomorph e`.
- Dilation formula: `dilation a t x = t⁻¹ • (x - a)` by `simp [dilation, dilationCLM, smul_sub]; abel`.
- Step 3: `rw [hdil, norm_smul, norm_inv, Real.norm_of_nonneg ht.le, inv_mul_lt_iff₀ ht]` after `rw [mem_ball, dist_eq_norm] at hx`, then `linarith`.
- Step 4: `|d|` is a.e.-strongly measurable via `hdm.norm`.

- Step 6: `integral_sub` and `abs_integral_le_integral_abs`.
- Step 7: `gcongr`, then `(ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos ht2).symm`, then `congr 1; rw [abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ t⁻¹ ^ 2)]; field_simp`.
proof_key_steps: h := ϑ∘dilation a t is continuous with compact support (dilation a t is a homeomorphism), hence μ-integrable; h ≥ 0 and h = 1 on B_{3t}(a).
h·d, h·|d| and h(1 − |d|) are integrable, being dominated by h a.e. since |d| ≤ 1 a.e.; and h(1 − |d|) ≥ 0 a.e.
∫⁻_{B_{3t}(a)} ofReal(1 − |d|) dμ ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(h(1 − |d|)) dμ = ofReal(∫ h(1 − |d|) dμ).
Divide by ofReal(t²): ofReal(D)/ofReal(t²) = ofReal(t⁻²∫ h − |t⁻²∫ h·d|).

subproblems.title: Test forms correspond under η_{x,λ}, and η_{x,λ#}T(ω) = λ^{−n}T(ω∘η)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary subset, x ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 and η = η_{x,λ} (η(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x), Contract `dilation x λ`). Then (a) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) there is ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y ∈ ℝ^P; (b) for every ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) there is ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y; (c) for every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)), ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y, the blow-up satisfies η_{x,λ#}T(ω) = λ^{−n}·T(ω'). Here 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n and η_{x,λ#}T = blowUp T x λ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam), (∀ ω : TestFormOn (dilation x lam '' U) n, ∃ ω' : TestFormOn U n, ∀ y : Euclid P, (ω' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y = (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (dilation x lam y)) ∧ (∀ ω' : TestFormOn U n, ∃ ω : TestFormOn (dilation x lam '' U) n, ∀ y : Euclid P, (ω' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y = (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (dilation x lam y)) ∧ ∀ (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn (dilation x lam '' U) n) (ω' : TestFormOn U n), (∀ y : Euclid P, (ω' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y = (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (dilation x lam y)) → blowUp T x lam hlam.ne' ω = lam⁻¹ ^ n * T ω'

Source: parent proof step 0(ii) (pullback by η_{x,λ}); Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 (push-forward f_#T(ω) = T(f^#ω), chapter-06.txt lines 405–418).
Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P. For x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0, η := η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − x), and ι(z) := x + λz. For V ⊆ ℝ^P (any subset), 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n is the set of C^∞ maps ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (n-covectors) with compact topological support tsupport ω ⊆ V; elements of 𝒟ⁿ(V) are determined by their underlying forms. η_#Y := η_{x,λ#}Y = blowUp Y x λ for Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U). By the Contract definition of blowUp, for T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) we have η_#T(ω) = T(ν), where ν ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) has underlying form ν(y) = ω(−λ⁻¹x + L y) ∘ L with L := λ⁻¹·id (= dilationCLM P λ), i.e. ν(y)(v₁,…,vₙ) = ω(η(y))(λ⁻¹v₁,…,λ⁻¹vₙ) (SimonGMT affinePullbackForm L (−λ⁻¹x) ω; it is a test form in η⁻¹(η(U)) and is regarded as a test form in U through the inclusion η⁻¹(η(U)) ⊆ U, which does not change the underlying form).
1. η is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse ι. Indeed η is the composition of y ↦ λ⁻¹y (a homeomorphism since λ⁻¹ ≠ 0) with the translation z ↦ z − λ⁻¹x, and η(ι(z)) = λ⁻¹(x + λz − x) = z, ι(η(y)) = x + λ·λ⁻¹(y − x) = y. Both η and ι are affine, hence C^∞. In particular η is injective, so η⁻¹(η(V)) = V for every V ⊆ ℝ^P.
2. Two facts about supports. Let h : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be continuous and f : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P). (i) tsupport(f∘h) ⊆ h⁻¹(tsupport f): the set h⁻¹(tsupport f) is closed and contains {f∘h ≠ 0} = h⁻¹{f ≠ 0}. (ii) If h is a homeomorphism and f has compact support, then f∘h has compact support: h⁻¹(tsupport f) is compact (it is the image of the compact set tsupport f under the continuous inverse of h), and tsupport(f∘h) is a closed subset of it by (i).
3. Proof of (a). Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) and put ω' := ω∘η. Then ω' is C^∞ (composition of C^∞ maps), has compact support by 2(ii), and tsupport ω' ⊆ η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ η⁻¹(η(U)) = U by 2(i) and step 1. Hence ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for every y by definition.
4. Proof of (b). Let ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and put ω := ω'∘ι. Then ω is C^∞, has compact support by 2(ii) (ι is a homeomorphism), and tsupport ω ⊆ ι⁻¹(tsupport ω') ⊆ ι⁻¹(U). If ι(z) ∈ U then z = η(ι(z)) ∈ η(U); hence tsupport ω ⊆ η(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)). Finally ω(η(y)) = ω'(ι(η(y))) = ω'(y) for every y.
5. Proof of (c). Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) and ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y, and let ν be the test form in the definition of η_#T(ω). Note −λ⁻¹x + L y = η(y). Fix y and v₁,…,vₙ ∈ ℝ^P and put α := ω(η(y)) ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P). Since α is multilinear, α(λ⁻¹v₁,…,λ⁻¹vₙ) = (∏_{i=1}^{n} λ⁻¹)·α(v₁,…,vₙ) = λ^{−n}·α(v₁,…,vₙ) (for n = 0 the empty product is 1 = λ⁰). Hence ν(y) = λ^{−n}ω(η(y)) = λ^{−n}ω'(y) for all y, so ν = λ^{−n}ω' as elements of 𝒟ⁿ(U). By linearity of T, η_#T(ω) = T(ν) = T(λ^{−n}ω') = λ^{−n}·T(ω'). This proves (a), (b), (c) for arbitrary U and n. ∎
Formalization notes (this exact statement was proved in a scratch build): unfold blowUp, then rewrite with GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward_apply and GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply; reduce to an equality of underlying forms (Subtype.ext, funext, ext v) and use testFormOnInclusion_coe, affinePullbackTestOn_coe, affinePullbackForm, ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ, Finset.prod_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, then map_smul and smul_eq_mul. For (a), (b) build ⟨f, h⟩ after `change IsTestForm f ∧ tsupport f ⊆ V`, using HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph for the homeomorphisms (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ⁻¹ _).trans (Homeomorph.addLeft (−(λ⁻¹ • x))) (coercion = dilation x λ) and (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ _).trans (Homeomorph.addLeft x), together with tsupport_comp_subset_preimage and Set.preimage_image_eq. Under `open scoped ENNReal` the symbol ∞ is ENNReal's top, so write the smoothness order as ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞).
proof_key_steps: η is an affine homeomorphism with inverse ι(z) = x + λz; composition with a homeomorphism preserves smoothness and compact support, and tsupport(f∘h) ⊆ h⁻¹(tsupport f).
(a) ω' := ω∘η is a test form with tsupport ⊆ η⁻¹(η(U)) = U.
(b) ω := ω'∘ι is a test form with tsupport ⊆ ι⁻¹(U) ⊆ η(U), and ω∘η = ω'.
(c) The pulled-back form is ω(η(y))∘(λ⁻¹·id) = λ^{−n}ω(η(y)) = λ^{−n}ω'(y) by multilinearity; linearity of T gives η_#T(ω) = λ^{−n}T(ω').

subproblems.title: Basic properties of the weight measure θHᵏ⌞M of an IMRep: absolute continuity both ways, formula on Borel sets, local finiteness, and R.action ω = ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ ℝ^P (no openness is assumed) and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in W (IMRep W k): M = R.carrier is a Borel set with M ⊆ W, θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable with θ(x) ≥ 1 for x ∈ M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W, and ξ = R.orient : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M; here Hᵏ = μHE[k], R.measure = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ (the weight θHᵏ⌞M, contract IMRep.measure) and R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x) (contract IMRep.action). Then: (a) R.measure ≪ Hᵏ⌞M; (b) Hᵏ⌞M ≪ R.measure; (c) R.measure(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dHᵏ (lower Lebesgue integral of the [0,∞]-valued cast of θ) for every Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P; (d) R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0; (e) R.measure(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W; (f) ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for R.measure; (g) for every k-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ^k(ℝ^P) (an arbitrary DifferentialForm; no smoothness or integrability is assumed), R.action ω = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep W k), R.measure ≪ μHE[k].restrict R.carrier ∧ μHE[k].restrict R.carrier ≪ R.measure ∧ (∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → R.measure A = ∫⁻ x in R.carrier ∩ A, (R.mult x : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μHE[k]) ∧ R.measure R.carrierᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ W → R.measure K < ∞) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable R.orient R.measure ∧ ∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k, R.action ω = ∫ x, R.orient x (ω x) ∂R.measure

Source: the identities R.measure = θHᵏ⌞M and 'R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ = ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure (integral against a measure with density)' stated in the preamble of the selected node's proof and used in its steps 5–9. They are needed by the selected node itself (steps 5 and 6: finiteness of R_x.measure on compact sets, measurability of ξ_x for R_x.measure, transport of (IMC)(d), and R_x.action(ω) = ∫ ξ_x(ω) dR_x.measure) and by the sibling glue (steps 7–9).
Notation: ν := Hᵏ⌞M = μHE[k].restrict M and g(x) := θ(x) ∈ [0, ∞], so that R.measure = ν.withDensity g by the definition IMRep.measure.
1. g is measurable: θ is measurable (field measurable_mult of R), and the cast ℕ → [0, ∞] is measurable because every map out of ℕ is.
2. Proof of (c). Let A be Borel. By the definition of a measure with density, R.measure(A) = ∫_A g dν = ∫ g d(ν⌞A) (Mathlib withDensity_apply, A measurable). Since A is measurable, ν⌞A = (Hᵏ⌞M)⌞A = Hᵏ⌞(A ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Hence R.measure(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dHᵏ.
3. Proof of (d). ℝ^P ∖ M is Borel because M is (field measurableSet_carrier). By (c), R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ M) = ∫_{M ∩ (ℝ^P∖M)} θ dHᵏ = ∫_∅ θ dHᵏ = 0.
4. Proof of (e). Let K ⊆ W be compact. K is closed, hence Borel, so by (c) R.measure(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ, and this is finite by the field locallyIntegrable_mult of R applied to the compact set K ⊆ W.
5. Proof of (a). Let A ⊆ ℝ^P with ν(A) = 0, and choose a Borel set A' ⊇ A with ν(A') = 0 (a measurable hull). Then ν⌞A' is the zero measure, so R.measure(A') = ∫_{A'} g dν = 0, and R.measure(A) ≤ R.measure(A') = 0. Hence R.measure ≪ ν (Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous).
6. Proof of (b). First, g(x) ≠ 0 for ν-a.e. x: ν-a.e. x lies in M (ν(ℝ^P ∖ M) = Hᵏ((ℝ^P ∖ M) ∩ M) = Hᵏ(∅) = 0; Mathlib ae_restrict_mem, M Borel), and for x ∈ M, g(x) = θ(x) ≥ 1 (field mult_pos). Now let R.measure(A) = 0 and choose a Borel set A' ⊇ A with R.measure(A') = 0 (a measurable hull). Then ∫_{A'} g dν = 0, so g = 0 holds (ν⌞A')-a.e. (Mathlib lintegral_eq_zero_iff, g measurable). Together with g ≠ 0 ν-a.e. this gives (ν⌞A')(ℝ^P) = 0, i.e. ν(A') = 0, hence ν(A) = 0. So ν ≪ R.measure (this is Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous', whose hypotheses are exactly that g is a.e. measurable and g ≠ 0 ν-a.e.).
7. Proof of (f). ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for ν (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient). By (a), R.measure ≪ ν, and a.e. strong measurability passes to absolutely continuous measures (Mathlib AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac). Hence ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for R.measure.
8. Proof of (g). Let ω be any k-form and h(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)) ∈ ℝ. Put f(x) := (θ(x) : ℝ≥0), a measurable ℝ≥0-valued function whose cast to [0, ∞] is g, so R.measure = ν.withDensity (x ↦ (f(x) : [0,∞])). By Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul (for a measurable ℝ≥0-valued density f and an arbitrary function h, ∫ h d(ν.withDensity f) = ∫ f • h dν; no integrability assumption is needed, because h is integrable for ν.withDensity f exactly when f·h is integrable for ν, and both Bochner integrals are 0 otherwise), ∫ h dR.measure = ∫ f(x)·h(x) dν(x) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x), using f(x) • h(x) = (θ(x) : ℝ)·h(x). The right-hand side is R.action ω by the definition IMRep.action. ∎
proof_key_steps: R.measure = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ with θ measurable; withDensity_apply and restrict_restrict give R.measure(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dHᵏ for Borel A, hence R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0 and, by local integrability of θ, R.measure(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ W.
A measure with density is absolutely continuous with respect to its base measure; conversely θ ≥ 1 on M makes the density a.e. nonzero, so Hᵏ⌞M ≪ R.measure.
A.e. strong measurability of ξ passes from Hᵏ⌞M to R.measure by absolute continuity.
integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul turns ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure into ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ = R.action ω for every form ω.
